scope: Qualified periodic Qwen3.8 27B offered-load case and bounded verifier generalization

analysis_plan.scope: Fixed offered-load finite two-minute experiment; observed stability must be established, not presumed.
analysis_plan.steady_window_rule: Half-open window spanning four complete three-wave prompt-class cycles after the first cycle.
analysis_plan.queue_sample_rule: Use offers strictly before the boundary; compare unfinished and not-yet-admitted counts at equivalent cycle phase.
metrics: Full-run delivered output rate and elapsed time
Output rate and token-gap p50/p95/p99 within the fixed steady window
TTFT and admission delay for the predeclared balanced middle 48 requests
Per-wave and per-prompt-class TTFT, token-gap distributions and pending requests
Peak live slots, created/reused/discarded leases, final zero leases and retained KV payload
Per-width pure decode distributions, with actual context/schedule differences explicit
analysis_plan.comparisons: Report both original DA8 and RR256 settings. For within-5% serving comparisons, retain the best measured original value for each metric rather than selecting the slower configuration.
nonclaims: Fixed offered-load throughput does not establish maximum engine throughput.
No new isolated prefill-throughput or matched-context decode-kernel parity claim.
Unbounded queue stability and total VRAM budgeting are not proved by a finite run or KV payload alone.
Native numerical correctness remains unqualified until every distinct observed geometry is independently checked with original model math and full heads.

independent_full_heads.scope: Direct immutable original matrix bytes and every sampled row hash; avoids existing manifest validator hardcoded64 output precondition. Does not modify or relax any oracle/math comparison.

rr256.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition

da8.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition

comparison: Same GGUF checkpoint, BF16 activations, F32 recurrent state, disabled CUDA graphs, 8192 context cap, eight-live limit, four prefill lanes, chunk64 and overall budget256. Native mixed cap8; originals use DA8 and RR256 respectively. Original runs warm up on the same workload before three measured samples.
preserved_initial_failures: Controlled accounting validator incorrectly required actual peak to equal upper live limit; changed to a bounded actual peak independently checked against admission/completion timestamps and pool allocation.

General reference validator incorrectly required64 outputs, despite serving protocol supporting1..256. General histories now validate uniform1..256 counts; standalone BMS1 retains64 outputs/16requests/256steps and frozen SHA.
All8400 full-head matrices matched immutable original bytes before either validator change; no oracle or arithmetic policy was altered.
limitations: Two-minute periodic finite arrivals, with complete drains between native waves; native has zero mixed prefill/decode steps. This does not qualify sustained mixed serving or maximum capacity.
Fixed offered-load output throughput is constrained by the workload; no new isolated prefill throughput or matched-context decode-kernel claim.
KV payload only is reported; model, recurrent state, activation/workspace, driver and allocator storage are outside that native quota. Total device-memory budgeting remains open.
Native maximum live limit is eight but actual peak is four; original schedulers may keep more requests active because their execution geometry differs.
Performance original schedulers are unmodified; the separate FIFO host-selection adapter is numerical-control-only, with original model/worker/math/sampling/KV.
No native/original free-clock token equality is assumed when their schedules differ. All native timing schedules and tokens match the independent controlled full-head reference.
Network serving, unbounded queue stability, larger mixed/staggered workloads and the complete modern-model goal remain open.
